title: Investor styles
summary: How 30 well-known investors, fund managers and finance personalities actually invest or trade, one profile each, with a primer per style for the background.
intro: Thirty names, from fund managers with decades of audited returns to television personalities and convicted fraudsters. Each profile answers the same questions: where the returns came from, how ideas are found and sized, how losses are handled, what the record really is, and what an individual can and cannot take from it.
Names are grouped by style so the background is learned once. Each style has a primer that explains its instruments and vocabulary from zero. The profiles then assume only the primer.

Every profile ends with the same section: what carries over to long-term investing, to swing trading over days and weeks, and to day trading. A ranking of all 30, with stated criteria, comes last, once every record has been checked.

groups.title: Global macro
groups.blurb: Top-down bets on currencies, interest rates, stock indexes and commodities.

groups.title: Value and long-term equity
groups.blurb: Buying businesses below what they are worth and holding them.

groups.title: Quantitative and multi-strategy
groups.blurb: Models, data and many small bets; market making and pods of traders.

groups.title: Activist and concentrated bets
groups.blurb: A few large positions, and public pressure on management to change course.

groups.title: Distressed debt and event-driven
groups.blurb: Buying the bonds and shares of companies in trouble, and trading around bankruptcies and bailouts.

groups.title: Contrarian and short-selling
groups.blurb: Betting against a crowded view, including betting on prices to fall.

groups.title: Thematic growth funds
groups.blurb: Public funds built around one idea about the future, bought through an ETF.

groups.title: Venture capital and angel investing
groups.blurb: Stakes in young private companies, where a few winners pay for all the losers.

groups.title: Crypto trading and advocacy
groups.blurb: Exchanges, tokens and the people who promote them.

groups.title: Real estate and financial education
groups.blurb: Property bought with borrowed money, and the business of teaching it.

groups.title: Gold and bearish commentary
groups.blurb: A standing forecast of crisis, and the assets sold alongside it.

groups.title: Media and retail-facing personalities
groups.blurb: People whose business is attention, measured against what their picks did.

groups.title: Fraud case studies
groups.blurb: How each scheme worked, who was fooled, and which warning signs were visible at the time.
